subject: Affordability snapshot & action map from today's call
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Turner <ava.turner@ledgerlane.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Affordability snapshot & action map from today's call

Thanks again for taking time today, Ava — good conversation. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain you described:
- Unpredictable token spend from bursts (search + chat) during peak hours; current infra charges spike ~3x on Mondays.
- Strict monthly budget cap for experimentation: $12k run-rate for inference spend. Any pilot must fit or show immediate offsets.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 220ms for user-facing chat routes.

Goals you stated:
- Validate a production-friendly pilot that reduces per-interaction cost by >=40% via batching + prefix KV caching while meeting latency targets.
- Baseline token economics and a short ROI case for the execs by end of next month.

What we propose (pilot snapshot):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week setup, 4-week data/traffic validation).
- Scope: 3 endpoints (chat-short, chat-long, search).
- Levers: continuous batching, prefix KV cache for repeated prompts, and a conservative quantized model for search-only traffic.
- Hypothesis: blending batching (expected 25–45% token reduction depending on concurrency) + KV cache (15–30% fewer tokens on repeat flows) will net >=40% at steady state.

Immediate asks from LedgerLane (what we need to run a tight ROI):
1) Representative traffic dump (7 days) + sample prompts for chat/search (anonymized).
2) A primary technical contact and an LF for data access/ingestion (SFTP or GCS).
3) Confirmation that the $12k/month pilot cap is a hard limit for initial approval.

Deliverables we'll provide:
- Token econ snapshot (attached) with conservative/likely/upside scenarios.
- Pilot scope workbook (attached) with milestones, success criteria (cost delta, P95 latency), and rollback plan.
- Weekly readouts in the Redwood Console + a final ROI memo summarizing unit economics.

Next steps / timeline:
- You share traffic sample + tech contact by EOD Fri (2027-04-16).
- We ship an SOW draft + pilot workbook by Tue 2027-04-20.
- Kickoff tentatively week of 2027-04-26 pending access.

If the monthly cap is inflexible, we can scope a smaller initial experiment (search-only) to get early wins inside $12k — noted as an alternate in the attached workbook.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if any of this needs rework.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: pilot_scope.xlsx (workbook), token_econ_snapshot.pdf (summary)
From: Ava Turner <ava.turner@ledgerlane.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 19:02:00 +0000

Jonas — thanks for the crisp write-up. Quick clarifications: 
- Budget cap is firm for initial exec approval (we can stretch after we show clear offsets).
- Traffic dump: I can pull an anonymized gzip and drop it to the SFTP by Friday morning. I'll include a short doc explaining peak windows.
- Tech contact: looping in Legal for a quick review of the SFTP access form (CC'd legal@ledgerlane.com).

One ask from our side: can you include a conservative latency plan if batching introduces tail latency? Our app has hard P95 requirements; we need the mitigation checklist spelled out in the SOW.

Also, if the pilot demonstrates >30% savings we can fast-track a longer evaluation.

I'll confirm by Friday on the data drop.

— Ava
Ava Turner
Head of ML Platform, LedgerLane
ava.turner@ledgerlane.com

Ava — adding a few pricing/ops clarifications from Redwood side: 
- Pricing model for pilot: we can run pilot under a capped pilot invoice with token-level reporting; if savings materialize we'll offer a stepped credit structure in month 2 to offset onboarding costs (details in SOW).
- Ops: we'll enable route-level tracing and a temporary higher retention window for traces so we can correlate token patterns to latency.
- Latency mitigations: we include an explicit fallback policy (route-level) to bypass batching for requests that exceed an internal P95 threshold; we also set conservative batch timers initially (e.g., 8ms) and iterate.

Jonas — I'll draft the SOW language around the credit and fallback policy and include it in the Tue deliverable.

Marissa
